Day 2 Convective Outlook CORR 1
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0130 AM CDT Sat Aug 08 2026

Valid 091200Z - 101200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
THE MIDWEST...

CORRECTED FOR THUNDERLINE

...SUMMARY...
Thunderstorms with severe wind gusts will be possible Sunday
afternoon and evening from parts of the northern Plains
east-southeastward into the southern Great Lakes. Severe gusts will
also be possible in parts of the southern Appalachians, Maine and
southeast Arizona.

...Northern Plains/Mid To Upper Mississippi Valley/Southern Great
Lakes...
Mid-level flow will be west-northwesterly on Sunday from the
northern Plains into the Great Lakes. At the surface, a moist and
unstable airmass will be in place from South Dakota eastward into
the southern Great Lakes. Although moderate instability is forecast
to develop over much of this corridor by afternoon, large-scale
ascent will remain relatively weak. For that reason, thunderstorm
development will confined to areas where low-level convergence
becomes maximized. Some solutions show an east-to-west axis of
strong low-level convergence from Iowa into northern Indiana,
suggesting this could be a favored area for thunderstorm development
in the afternoon and evening. 

Forecast soundings near this axis in the late afternoon have surface
dewpoints in the 70s with moderate to strong instability. 0-6 km
shear is forecast to be in the 35 to 45 knot range with a
substantial amount of low-level directional shear. This should
support a severe threat with supercells and short intense line
segments. Severe wind gusts will be the primary threat.

Further west into parts of the northern Plains, a subtle shortwave
trough is forecast to move into South Dakota during the day. A
post-frontal airmass will be in place ahead of the shortwave with
surface dewpoints in the 60s to near 70 F. This will contribute to
moderate instability by afternoon. Thunderstorms that develop near
the axis of instability will have potential for isolated severe
gusts during the late afternoon and early evening.

...Maine...
A mid-level shortwave trough is forecast to move across the Great
Lakes on Sunday, with west-southwesterly flow located over the
Northeast. Ahead of the system, a cold front is forecast to move
eastward across New England. As surface temperatures warm during the
day, thunderstorm development is expected to take place near the
front in the higher terrain across parts of western Maine. These
storms are forecast to move quickly eastward across central and
eastern Maine during the afternoon. Moderate instability, steep low
lapse rates and sufficient deep-layer shear will likely support an
isolated wind-damage threat.

...Southern Appalachians...
Moderate instability will develop on Sunday across much of the
southern Appalachians, where surface dewpoints will be in the upper
60s to mid 70s F. As surface temperatures warm during the day,
scattered thunderstorms will develop in the higher terrain. The
moderate instability, along with precipitable water values in the
1.70 to 1.85 inch range, will support a potential for isolated
severe wet downbursts as instability becomes maximized in the late
afternoon.

...Southeast Arizona...
Surface dewpoints across southern Arizona will be in the upper 50s
to near 60 F on Sunday. As surface temperatures warm during the day,
moderate instability will develop over much of southern Arizona.
Thunderstorms are expected to form in the higher terrain of eastern
Arizona, with the storms moving west-southwestward into the unstable
air during the late afternoon and early evening. Steep low-level
lapse rates and large surface temperature-dewpoint spreads will
support an isolated wind-damage threat.

..Broyles.. 08/08/2026

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0220 AM CDT Sat Aug 08 2026

Valid 101200Z - 111200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM PARTS OF
NORTHERN ILLINOIS EAST-SOUTHEASTWARD INTO WESTERN PENNSYLVANIA...

...SUMMARY...
Thunderstorms with severe wind gusts will be possible on Monday from
parts of northern Illinois eastward into western Pennsylvania.
Isolated severe gusts will also be possible from parts of the
central and northern Plains into the Midwest.

...Southern Great Lakes...
A mid-level shortwave trough will move into the Great Lakes region
on Monday. At the surface, a quasi-stationary front is forecast to
be located from northern Illinois eastward into northwestern
Pennsylvania. Surface dewpoints to the south of the front are
forecast to be in the 70s F, which will contribute to moderate
destabilization by midday. Scattered thunderstorms appear likely to
develop near the front by early afternoon, with the storms moving
southeastward into the unstable air. To the south of the front,
MLCAPE is forecast to peak in the 2000 to 3000 J/kg range. In
addition, the models show moderate deep-layer shear in place which
will most likely support a mixed mode, with supercells and short
intense line segments capable of severe wind gusts. The severe
threat could continue into the mid to late evening if a cold pool
can become established and persist.

...Central and Northern Plains/Midwest...
West-northwesterly mid-level flow will be in place over much of the
north-central U.S. on Monday. At the surface, a low is forecast to
deepen over South Dakota as a cold front moves through the northern
Plains. To the south of the front, an axis of strong instability
appears likely to develop by afternoon from northern Nebraska
eastward into Iowa, where model forecasts suggest that MLCAPE could
peak in the in the 3500 to 4500 J/kg range. In addition, forecast
soundings show directional shear in the low to mid-levels, which
will contribute to moderate deep-layer shear over much of the moist
sector. This environment should support an isolated severe threat
during the late afternoon and early evening. Due to relatively weak
large-scale ascent, convective coverage is expected to be isolated,
with any severe threat remaining localized.

..Broyles.. 08/08/2026

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0355 AM CDT Sat Aug 08 2026

Valid 111200Z - 161200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...Tuesday/Day 4 and Wednesday/Day 5...
A broad cyclonic mid-level flow pattern is forecast from the upper
Mississippi Valley into the Northeast on Tuesday and Wednesday. At
the surface, a moist airmass is forecast to be in place over most of
the eastern half of the nation with a quasi-stationary front located
from the northern Plains east-southeastward into the southern Great
Lakes. To the south of the front, surface dewpoints in the 70s F
will likely result in the development of moderate to strong
instability. Isolated to scattered thunderstorms appear likely to
develop each afternoon in areas where low-level convergence becomes
maximized. Outflow boundaries will be important in determining where
the greatest convective coverage ends up being. In addition to the
instability, moderate deep-layer shear is forecast over much of this
moist airmass suggesting that an isolated wind-damage threat will be
possible. However, the lack of any appreciable mid-level shortwave
trough introduces considerable uncertainty.

...Thursday/Day 6 and Saturday/Day 8...
From Thursday to Saturday, mid-level flow is forecast to become
westerly over much of the northern U.S, with a front located from
the central Plains eastward into the southern Great Lakes and Ohio
Valley. Thunderstorm development will be possible each afternoon and
evening near this front. Surface dewpoints in the 70s F to the south
of the front, along with moderate to strong instability will make
isolated severe thunderstorms possible each afternoon and evening.
However, spatial uncertainty concerning any potential severe threat
is considerable at this range.

..Broyles.. 08/08/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0743 AM CDT Sat Aug 08 2026

Valid 081300Z - 091200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM NORTHERN
PARTS OF THE MID-ATLANTIC INTO SOUTHERN PORTIONS OF THE NORTHEAST...

...SUMMARY...
Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms capable primarily of
damaging gusts will be possible today across the Mid-Atlantic states
into southern New England.

...Mid-Atlantic states into southern New England...
Satellite imagery this morning indicates a weak disturbance moving
east across the Lower Great Lakes, with early morning
showers/thunderstorms from WV/PA into western NY likely associated
with this feature.  Strong heating from Chesapeake Bay northward
into southern portions of the Northeast will yield around 2000 J/kg
MLCAPE by early afternoon.  Of particular note is seemingly adequate
strength of flow between 700-250 mb for organized line segments. 
Given the relatively high PW environment (1.75-2.0 inches),
expecting a few clusters to evolve this afternoon with an attendant
risk for strong to locally severe gusts (50-65 mph).  Have
expanded/increased severe-wind probabilities into southern New
England and southward into the Chesapeake Bay vicinity.  Marginally
severe hail may also occur with the stronger cells before excessive
outflow leads to more linear structures as this activity pushes east
towards the coast by the early evening.

...Northern/Central Plains into MN/IA/MO...
Radar/satellite mosaic shows a cluster of strong to locally severe
thunderstorms over the NE Sandhills this morning.  This activity may
continue southeast this morning but weaken as it moves across
central NE.  Above average uncertainty/low confidence for this
forecast is due in part to weak to negligible forcing features and
large model spread on potential evolution of isolated to widely
scattered storms later today into tonight.  Nonetheless, a strongly
unstable airmass is forecast to develop by early afternoon across
much of the region with 60s to lower 70s boundary layer dewpoints
beneath steep 700-500 mb lapse rates.  

Several areas of convection may develop during the late
afternoon/evening near the surface trough, and overnight near the
southward-sagging surface front.  Weak convergence along early day
outflow may rejuvenate convection or lead to additional isolated
storms over southern NE into northern KS.  This may also coincide
with an increasing low-level jet across the central Plains during
the evening into the overnight, but capping will likely limit storm
coverage except perhaps near a southward-sagging surface front near
the ND/SD border and with warm advection over southern MN into IA. 
Large hail and severe gusts will be possible with the more intense
thunderstorms.

Additional high-based convection is possible across eastern CO and
western KS/NE.  A hot and well mixed boundary layer will probably
support isolated severe gusts.  

...AZ...
Easterly midlevel flow will persist on the southern periphery of an
upper high over the Four Corners.  Steep midlevel lapse rates and
persistent moisture across the region will foster thunderstorm
development across the higher terrain during the evening.  The hot
and well mixed boundary layer will support strong outflow gusts as
convection moves westward off higher terrain toward the lower
deserts.

..Smith/Kerr.. 08/08/2026
